description: Run queue wait of each workload, the workloads that caused it, and checks that rule out other causes.

links.title: Dashboard notes
links.tooltip: How to read and import this dashboard

panels.description: Static notes. This panel runs no query.

options.content:
**Question:** does a workload wait for CPU, and is a neighbour the cause?

Read the rows from top to bottom:

1. **Start here** shows the worst wait in each cluster.
2. **Where** ranks the workloads and the nodes. Click a name to select it.
3. **Victim** shows the wait of the selected workload.
4. **Who** names the workloads that held the CPU, and the cause of the wait.
5. **Rule out** compares the wait with the CPU limit and the node pressure.
6. **Trust** shows the health of the agents. A gap there means that the rows above are not complete.

Amber starts at 100 µs and red at 1 ms. A task on an idle CPU waits a few µs. A task on a busy CPU waits for ms.

The file `deploy/dashboard/noisy-neighbour.json` is the source. UI edits do not survive the next import.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard

panels.description: The highest p99 run queue wait of a workload on a node, in each cluster. The synthetic `_system` and `_overflow` entities do not count. Amber starts at 100 µs and red at 1 ms.

targets.expr: max by (cluster) (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, node, namespace, workload_kind, workload, le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace!~"_.*"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Worst p99 wait

panels.description: The number of workloads with a p99 run queue wait above 1 ms on a node. A workload counts once for each node. The synthetic `_system` and `_overflow` entities do not count.

targets.expr: count(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, node, namespace, workload_kind, workload, le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace!~"_.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0.001) or vector(0)

panels.title: Over 1 ms per node

panels.description: The share of all run queue wait in each cluster with the cause `other_workload`. A neighbour held the CPU for this share. The synthetic `_system` and `_overflow` entities do not count.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_wait_by_cause_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace!~"_.*", cause="other_workload"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace!~"_.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Neighbour share

panels.description: The workloads ranked by their worst p99 run queue wait in the time range, with the mean wait. Both sum the nodes of a workload. Click a workload to select it. Amber starts at 100 µs and red at 1 ms.

targets.expr: max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, namespace, workload_kind, workload, le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:])

avg_over_time((sum by (cluster, namespace, workload_kind, workload) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, namespace, workload_kind, workload) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:])

panels.title: Workloads by wait

panels.description: The nodes ranked by the worst p99 run queue wait of the selected workloads in the time range, with the mean wait. Click a node to select it. Amber starts at 100 µs and red at 1 ms.

targets.expr: max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (cluster, node, le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:])

avg_over_time((sum by (cluster, node) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (cluster, node) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload"}[$__rate_interval])))[$__range:])

panels.title: Nodes by wait

panels.description: Run queue waits of the selected workloads per second, in the bucket of each wait. A move to the upper buckets means longer waits.

targets.expr: sum by (le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Wait distribution

panels.description: The mean run queue wait of the selected workloads. Amber starts at 100 µs and red at 1 ms.

targets.expr: sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_count{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean wait

panels.description: The p50 and p99 run queue wait of the selected workloads. The histogram has 8 buckets by default, so these values are coarse. Use them to rank and to see a trend, not as exact values. Amber starts at 100 µs and red at 1 ms.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p50 and p99 wait

panels.description: The share of the run queue wait of the selected workloads for each workload that held the CPU. `_other` sums the culprits with no series of their own. `_overflow` sums the workloads outside the series budget. The bars do not reach 100%, because idle and throttled wait has no culprit.

targets.expr: sum by (culprit_namespace, culprit_workload) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_wait_by_culprit_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Culprit share of wait

panels.description:
The share of the run queue wait of the selected workloads for each cause:

- `other_workload`: a neighbour held the CPU.
- `same_workload`: another task of the same workload held the CPU.
- `system`: a process outside the pods held the CPU.
- `idle`: the wait ended on an idle CPU.
- `throttled`: the CPU limit of the workload stopped it.

targets.expr: sum by (cause) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_wait_by_cause_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Wait by cause

panels.description: The throttled and idle share of the wait from the agent, against the share of CFS periods with throttle from cAdvisor. The agent does not export the cAdvisor series. If both throttle lines rise, the CPU limit of the workload causes the wait. cAdvisor has no workload label, so the query matches the pod names of each controller. A workload name with a last segment that looks like a hash, such as `web-7d9f8b`, can also match the pods of a shorter workload, such as `web`. Static pods do not match.

targets.expr: sum (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_wait_by_cause_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node", cause="throttled"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_wait_by_cause_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node", cause="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum(rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$workload(-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{6,10}-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{5}|-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{5}|-[0-9]+|-[0-9]+-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{5})?", node=~"$node", container!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum(rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$workload(-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{6,10}-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{5}|-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{5}|-[0-9]+|-[0-9]+-[bcdfghjklmnpqrstvwxz2456789]{5})?", node=~"$node", container!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Throttled and idle share against CFS throttle

panels.description: The share of time in which at least one task on the node waited for CPU, from the PSI of node exporter. The agent does not export this series. Pressure on all nodes points to a lack of CPU, not to one neighbour.

targets.expr: avg by (cluster, node) (rate(node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Node CPU pressure

panels.description: The p99 run queue wait of the selected workloads on the left axis, and the share of the wait with the cause `other_workload` on the right axis. If both rise together, a neighbour causes the wait.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

sum (rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_wait_by_cause_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node", cause="other_workload"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(sum(rate(noisy_neighbour_runqueue_latency_seconds_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", workload=~"$workload", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p99 wait against neighbour share

panels.description: Static notes. This panel runs no query.

options.content:
Compare the panels of this row over the same time range.

- **Neighbour:** the neighbour share rises with the p99 wait. **Who** names the culprit.
- **Self:** the throttled share or the CFS throttle rises. The CPU limit of the workload is too low.
- **Unclear:** neither rises. Look at the node pressure and the idle share. A high idle share points to the wakeup path, not to a neighbour.

panels.title: Verdict

panels.description: The per entity series of each agent as a share of its series budget. At 90%, the agent stops new culprit series. At 100%, new workloads go to `_overflow`.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, node) (noisy_neighbour_series{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"} / noisy_neighbour_series_budget{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})

panels.title: Series against the budget

panels.description: The workloads in `_overflow` on each node, because they did not fit in the series budget. Their wait shows only under `_overflow`. The healthy value is 0.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, node) (noisy_neighbour_overflow_workloads{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})

panels.title: Overflow workloads

panels.description: The cgroups with samples that wait for the pod watch on each node. A value that stays above 0 means that the agent cannot name some pods.

targets.expr: max by (cluster, node) (noisy_neighbour_unresolved_cgroups{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})

panels.title: Unresolved cgroups

panels.description: Samples per second that the agent lost because a BPF map was full. `runq` is the cgroup map and `pairs` is the culprit pair map. The healthy value is 0.

targets.expr: sum by (cluster, node, map) (rate(noisy_neighbour_dropped_samples_total{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Dropped samples

panels.description: The number of agents that run each version. More than one row means that a rollout is in progress or stuck.

targets.expr: count by (cluster, version, git_sha) (noisy_neighbour_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster", node=~"$node"})
